title: `merge --lane-lint` runs inside a worktree-isolated agent
why: `merge --lane-lint` is refused inside a worktree-isolated agent, so lane item-cite-carries-name (#1790) ran ci-job --lint and ste-changed instead, and runner 8 reruns lane lint (coordinator, 23:29 CST Nov 7). Other lane sessions ran it from their main checkout. Sighting 01:35 CST Nov 14 (lane combine-g1, cloud session, worktree combine-g1e, via the coordinator 01:27; text relayed, unread by triage): `python3 merge/merge.py 3373 --lane-lint` refused two ways. (1) Foreground, timeout 600000 ms, PreToolUse:Bash check-timeout: "a lane lint with a time limit shorter than its own bound ends before it prints a verdict (decision background-check-through-verdict) ... Remedy: start it in the background, as `verdict <cmd>`, with a time limit of at least 3900000 ms ... To allow this act, type `override` for this one act, or `override 15m` for every refused act for 15 minutes." (2) Background, timeout 3900000, refused twice: "This session is isolated in the worktree ... but this command is too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree. Refusing to run it ... Split it into plain, separate commands and run them from ..." The command had no git and no chain. Result: the lane lint has no path in a cloud worktree session; the coordinator routed #3373's lint to runner 10's session. This is the step's own case, now with a combined PR (30 members) waiting on it.
note: Scope unchecked: triage did not find the refusal's source on main (merge/merge.py makes its own detached worktree for lane lint, line 2405). First prove the refusal happens only in an agent's isolated worktree, and name the guard or check that refuses it. Not a queue fix; waits under the item 384 hold. Slug from the coordinator; title by triage. Cause named (lane batch63-lint-b, coordinator 00:29 CST Nov 8): the refusal is Claude Code's own worktree check, not a repo hook. Covered by lane runner-repos-in-parallel, whose follow-up PR adds the brief-template line "the lane orchestrator runs --lane-lint, never an isolated builder". Sighting (lane encoded-retry-after-refusal, [ended:Lane:-encoded-retry-after-refusal], 17:28 CST Nov 8): in a session isolated in a worktree (EnterWorktree, .claude/worktrees/encoded-retry-merge), the harness refused three plain commands as "too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree": `python3 merge/merge.py --lane-lint 2314` (one command, worktree root, nothing chained), `~/.claude/bin/verdict ~/.claude/bin/merge --lane-lint 2314`, and the same after a cd into the worktree. The command names no git call; the merge tool runs git inside. The same command ran from the main checkout. Also on step harness-worktree-git-probe. Sighting (lane review-record-provenance, via the coordinator 05:11 CST Nov 9): in a session isolated in a worktree, the worktree-isolation check refused `merge --lane-lint <pr>` 3 times as too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree. The merge tool lints in its own temp worktree and is read-only (allow entry Merge Tool Read Checks). Ready, lane ended and not landed: no brief-template line 'never an isolated builder' in skills/project-ops/templates/brief.md on main; no PR (triage reader agent, Explore Sonnet audit, read of origin/main 0e6509a96, 06:03 CST Nov 10). Doing 06:06 CST Nov 10 in lane [ended:lane-lint-in-isolated-worktree] (coordinator). #2531 released to batch 72 (coordinator 07:01 CST Nov 10). MEASURED, cloud Claude Code 2.1.322, from inside an EnterWorktree session: `merge --lane-lint` was refused twice as a background Bash command ("too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree"), and accepted twice in the foreground (runs of 1102 s and about 1000 s). The refusal depends on how the command runs, not only on the worktree. Batch 72 (12:37 CST Nov 10): #2531 (3720c6b89, on main) put a workaround in the brief template (brief.md:33-36), because the refusal is Claude Code's own check. The title asks that lane lint runs inside an isolated worktree; that is not built, so the step stays open.
